messages:
sophia: nightdash just flagged a sustained p95/throughput drift starting ~03:12 UTC, looks correlated with last merge. https://nightdash.internal/redwood/alerts/rr-432 :eyes:
perf-bot: nightly SLO breach: p95 latency +17% vs baseline (window 03:00-04:00). run_id=rr-432, region=us-west2
kevin: i'm seeing the same on the perf heatmap — spike centered on batch size ~64 and a weird shift in kernel selection counts
anita: CI is throwing a few `end-to-end` perf failures after the merge too, e2e-p90 regressed in job 20260301T0315
jamal: starting a bisect across the last 8 merges (going to narrow to the 4 that touched scheduler/kernel_selector)
kevin: pulled a quick profile from the canary node (run canary-20260301-03). `perf top` shows a big increase in kernel selector time:
```
kernel_selector.go:matchKernelForBatch 32.4%
scheduler/batcher.go:coalesceBatches 18.1%
kv/cache.go:handleEviction         9.7%
other: remainder
```
anita: wow matchKernelForBatch jumped. that function got a small change in commit abcdef1 (batching heuristic + prefetch hint)
oliver: i repro'd locally with the exact canary config using `make perf-run` on merge/opt-scheduling; similar p95 shift 
jamal: bisect narrowed it to abcdef1 -> that commit toggled prefetch hints and bumped the selector epsilon for kernel weight balancing
sophia: release/34 rollout is on hold right? we shouldn't push until we have a mitigation
kevin: yes hold is still active. two short options: revert abcdef1 entirely or patch kernel selector to short-circuit the heavy path when sequence lengths < 256
anita: threw together a quick patch (PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/1234) — lowers selector aggressiveness and relaxes prefetch for small batches. no behavioral change for long sequences
perf-bot: triggered perf-run: rr-432-patch (canary) queued -> runner id rr-432-patch-1
jamal: running the patched canary now against the same workload, will post p95 numbers in a few minutes
kevin: posting the quick before/after from the canary run:
before patch: p95=184ms, throughput=156 req/s, kv_miss_rate=18%
after patch : p95=132ms, throughput=203 req/s, kv_miss_rate=4%

oliver: KV miss rate drop looks real — fewer handoffs and less cache churn after the selector change
sophia: nice. can we keep the patch minimal and roll forward once canary holds for 30m? :thumbsup:
kevin: plan: merge patch -> stage canary 10% -> monitor 30m -> roll forward. if any regressions revert the whole merge set (we'll keep abcdef1 revert as fallback)
ci-bot: deploybot: canary rollout to 10% started at 03:48 UTC for rr-432-patch-1
anita: adding an e2e perf test that exercises small-batch fast-paths so this doesn't regress again
jamal: i'll add a short-term alert on kernel_selector CPU share > 20% so nightdash will catch similar issues earlier
kevin: also adding a follow-up issue to tune the batcher thresholds and add a perf-test harness for mixed seq-length workloads
sophia: thanks all — please paste any flamegraphs/traces to this thread and i'll draft a short incident note for the release notes
oliver: posting flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/redwood/fg/rr-432-patch-1.html (reduced flame depth on selector path)
anita: cherry-picked the patch to a hotfix branch in case we need to fast revert upstream later
jamal: documenting root cause: combined heuristic change (abcde1) increased expensive kernel-selector path for small batches -> higher KV evictions -> tail latency and throughput degradation
sophia: good triage. once canary stable i'll remove hold and proceed with release. closing loop when documented in postmortem. :white_check_mark:
kevin: ack. will monitor the overnight dashboards and post if anything else pops up
